newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Mine blast in Burundi kills four, army says.
newsitem.headline: Mine blast in Burundi kills four, army says.

text.p: Four civilians were killed when a minibus hit an anti-tank mine on a main road south of Burundi's capital Bujumbura, an army spokesman said on Monday.
"A minibus travelling south on National Route Three towards Rumonge hit an anti-tank mine on Sunday," said army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi. "The explosion killed four people."

He blamed rebels of the main Hutu rebel National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) for planting the mine and said about 15 civilians were aboard the bus. He had no information on any wounded.
Nibizi said the mine exploded 40 km (25 miles) south of Bujumbura in Nyaruhongoka village.
Bujumbura residents said on Monday sporadic gunfire and mortar bomb explosions were audible in the capital over the weekend but the army said there were no casualties in clashes with rebels.
A Defence Ministry official said troops were involved in an operation in the area around Bujumbura against rebels moving from the northern province of Bubanza to the south of Burundi.
The CNDD, led by former interior minister Leonard Nyangoma, on Sunday condemned the execution of six people in Bujumbura and said it might pull out of peace talks scheduled for August 25.
The CNDD said the hangings of the six in Bujumbura's central prison on Thursday violated an agreement signed in Rome in March with the Burundi government on future peace negotiations.

The accord called for creation of an international crime tribunal to judge acts of genocide and other political crimes committed in Burundi, a former Belgian colony. The trials of the six men were carried by the local judicial authorities.
The six were accused of involvement in massacres in 1993.
More than 150,000 people have died in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the assassination of Burundi's first Hutu president in October 1993.
